Since e>0 there is positive area below -1, and h>2 gives points above -1. The cutting line therefore meets the interior. In particular 0<e<a, H>3 and Delta>0.

The predecessor upper-tail bound in the same coordinates is a-v-8a²/H² at level 2. Its complement is the area of the lower cap through level 2 because the level line has zero area, so that area is at most v+8a²/H².

The lower cap at -1 has area e and A has area a. The Minkowski average with weight 3/H on A lies in the lower cap at level 2 because -1+(3/H)(h+1)=2. The weight lies strictly between zero and one. Planar Brunn–Minkowski gives the asserted lower bound for the square root of the area.

Multiplication by positive H followed by squaring nonnegative quantities is reversible. The resulting cross term is -6 sqrt(e) Delta H, the square of the increment contributes -9 Delta², and the v and e terms give (v-e)H². Under v≤e and 8a²<9 Delta² the sum is strictly negative, proving impossibility, including the case v=e.

Independently checked the constant expansion with the unit-Jacobian rectangle |s|≤1/2, -2≤t≤7 and x=s-t/2, y=-s-t/2. It gives a=9, e=1, v=4, H=8, Delta=2. Both the squared-side difference and the expanded quadratic evaluate to 708.
